# pbs_metric_server_influxdb_http (Resource)

Manages a Proxmox Backup Server InfluxDB HTTP metric server: an InfluxDB server PBS sends its metrics to over HTTP or HTTPS, every 10 seconds — CPU, memory, network and disk usage of the host, and the usage of every datastore — with InfluxDB 2's write API, which InfluxDB 1.8 and 3 serve too.

~> **PBS checks the server before it saves anything.** On every create or update that leaves the server enabled — even one that changes only `comment` — PBS sends `GET <url>/health` from its own host, with the token, and needs a 2xx answer; otherwise the apply fails, with what to check, and nothing changes. The PBS host, not the machine running Terraform, must reach the server; PBS does not use the node's HTTP proxy for it, and waits as long as the connection takes, so a server that drops packets can outlast the provider's `request_timeout`. Set `enable = false` to save a server that is not reachable yet.

The check proves only that PBS reaches InfluxDB: it writes nothing, so it tests neither `organization` and `bucket` nor the token's write access, and InfluxDB 2 and 1.8 answer `/health` without looking at the token at all. A server that passes can still refuse every write; PBS logs that only in its journal, as `error sending to metric server <name>`.

InfluxDB HTTP and UDP metric servers share one namespace: `pbs_metric_server_influxdb_udp` cannot take this name. Managing metric servers needs `Sys.Modify on /`, reading them `Sys.Audit on /`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Send PBS's metrics to InfluxDB 2, into the bucket pbs of the organization
# ops, with a token that may write there. PBS checks the server — GET
# https://influxdb.example.com:8086/health — before it saves it, from its own
# host.
resource "pbs_metric_server_influxdb_http" "influxdb" {
  name         = "influxdb"
  url          = "https://influxdb.example.com:8086"
  organization = "ops"
  bucket       = "pbs"
  comment      = "Grafana dashboards"

  # The token is write-only: it never reaches the plan or state, and PBS
  # receives it when the server is created and whenever token_wo_version
  # changes.
  token_wo         = var.influxdb_token
  token_wo_version = 1
}

variable "influxdb_token" {
  description = "InfluxDB API token with write access to the bucket pbs."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  ephemeral   = true
}

# InfluxDB 1.8 behind a reverse proxy that serves it below /influxdb: its
# write API for InfluxDB 2 clients takes the database and retention policy as
# the bucket, and the user and password as the token. The proxy's certificate
# comes from an internal CA, which must be in the PBS host's trust store
# (/usr/local/share/ca-certificates, then update-ca-certificates): with
# verify_tls = false, PBS would send the password to whatever answers there.
resource "pbs_metric_server_influxdb_http" "legacy" {
  name             = "influxdb-legacy"
  url              = "https://metrics.example.com/influxdb"
  bucket           = "pbs/autogen"
  token_wo         = "pbs:${var.influxdb_legacy_password}"
  token_wo_version = 1
}

variable "influxdb_legacy_password" {
  description = "Password of the InfluxDB 1.8 user pbs."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  ephemeral   = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Metric server name, 3 to 32 characters: letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, not starting with `.` or `-`. InfluxDB HTTP and UDP servers share one namespace. Changing it replaces the server.
- `url` (String) Base URL of the InfluxDB server, such as `https://influxdb.example.com:8086`: `http://` or `https://`, the host, an optional port and an optional path, for a reverse proxy that serves InfluxDB below one. PBS appends `/health` and `/api/v2/write` to the URL's path, so leave out `/api/v2`.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `bucket` (String) InfluxDB bucket PBS writes the metrics to, up to 32 characters; for InfluxDB 1.8, `<database>/<retention policy>`, or the database. Defaults to `proxmox`.
- `comment` (String) Free-form comment, up to 128 characters on one line.
- `enable` (Boolean) Whether PBS sends its metrics to the server. PBS checks the URL only while the server is enabled: set `false` to save a server PBS cannot reach yet. Defaults to `true`.
- `max_body_size` (Number) Most bytes of metrics PBS sends in one request. Defaults to `25000000`.
- `organization` (String) InfluxDB organization the bucket belongs to, up to 32 characters; InfluxDB 1.8 ignores it. Defaults to `proxmox`.
- `token_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) API token PBS writes the metrics with, sent as `Authorization: Token <token>`: an InfluxDB 2 token with write access to `bucket`, or for InfluxDB 1.8, `<user>:<password>`. InfluxDB 2 and 3 take no write without one: leave it out only for a server that needs none, such as InfluxDB 1.8 without authentication. Removing it, with `token_wo_version`, leaves the token PBS has. Write-only: Terraform passes it to PBS without storing it in the plan or state, and PBS never returns it, so a change made outside Terraform goes unnoticed. PBS receives it when the object is created and whenever `token_wo_version` changes. Requires `token_wo_version`, and Terraform or OpenTofu 1.11 or later.
- `token_wo_version` (Number) Version of `token_wo`, which Terraform stores in its place. Change it — increment it, say — to send a new `token_wo`; removing it, with `token_wo`, leaves the value on the server as it is. Requires `token_wo`.
- `verify_tls` (Boolean) Whether PBS verifies the TLS certificate of an `https://` URL: it must be valid for the URL's host and signed by a CA the PBS host trusts, so an internal CA goes into the PBS host's trust store. With `false`, PBS accepts any certificate: the connection is encrypted, but whoever answers in the server's place gets the token. Defaults to `true`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same value as `name`, present because Terraform requires an `id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_metric_server_influxdb_http.influxdb
  identity = {
    name = "influxdb"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `name` (String) Metric server name, such as `influxdb`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_metric_server_influxdb_http.influxdb
  id = "influxdb"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# InfluxDB HTTP metric servers are imported by name, as Configuration →
# Metric Server in the web interface, or the pbs_metric_servers data source,
# shows it. PBS never returns the token, so token_wo_version is empty after an
# import: a configuration that sets it sends token_wo in the next apply,
# replacing the token PBS has, and PBS first checks an enabled server with
# that token. Leave token_wo and token_wo_version out to keep the token PBS
# has.
terraform import pbs_metric_server_influxdb_http.influxdb influxdb
```
